title: Voltora — E-Commerce Platform
subtitle: Full-stack online store with real Stripe checkout
description: Full-stack e-commerce solution with React, Node.js, and Stripe integration
longDescription: Voltora is a full-stack online store built with a decoupled architecture: a Node.js + Express + Prisma backend exposing a REST API, and a React + Vite frontend consuming it. The project includes a complete checkout flow integrated with Stripe, order management with multiple states (pending, paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded), and database-level stock control.

One of the aspects I focused on most was payment reliability: instead of trusting the browser redirect after payment — which can fail, be closed, or be spoofed — the real order status is only confirmed through a cryptographically verified Stripe webhook, while the frontend polls its own backend until that status changes. This prevents orders from ever being marked as paid without a genuine server-to-server confirmation.

highlights.title: Stripe Hosted Checkout
highlights.description: Chose Stripe's hosted payment page over embedded Elements to minimize PCI-compliance surface area and reduce implementation time.

highlights.title: Webhooks as the single source of truth
highlights.description: Order confirmation never depends on the success URL, which a user could manipulate — only on an HMAC-signature-verified Stripe webhook.

highlights.title: Idempotent checkout sessions
highlights.description: A client-generated Idempotency-Key prevents duplicate charges caused by double-clicks or network retries.

highlights.title: Atomic stock updates
highlights.description: Inventory is decremented with a database-level condition (stock >= quantity) to avoid race conditions when concurrent purchases hit the same product.

highlights.title: Automatic refunds on stock conflicts
highlights.description: If a payment is confirmed after stock ran out between session creation and confirmation, the system automatically refunds via the Stripe API and marks the order as refunded.

highlights.title: Environment validation with Zod
highlights.description: Critical environment variables, such as Stripe keys, are validated at server startup to avoid silent failures in production.

highlights.title: Dedicated webhook middleware
highlights.description: The Stripe endpoint uses express.raw() ahead of the global express.json(), a detail required for signature verification to work correctly.

title: Minimalist Three-Page Website
subtitle: A clean, reusable React + TypeScript template
description: Minimalist three-page website template with client-side routing and a clean, reusable layout
longDescription: This project is a minimalist three-page website built with React, TypeScript, and Vite, designed as a reusable starting point for personal projects, GitHub portfolios, and quick proof-of-concept sites. It ships with a Home, About Us, and Contact Us page connected through client-side routing, so navigating between them never triggers a full page reload.

The focus was on keeping the codebase small and easy to adapt: a single shared navbar layout wraps every page, animated with Framer Motion for hover and active-link effects, while each page itself stays a simple, self-contained component. It's meant to be forked and restyled quickly rather than extended into a large application.

highlights.title: Single shared layout
highlights.description: A NavbarLayout component wraps every route, so the navigation bar and page transitions stay consistent without duplicating markup across pages.

highlights.title: Animated navigation state
highlights.description: Framer Motion drives the active-route underline and link hover effects, and the mobile menu's open/close animation, using useLocation to track the current route.

highlights.title: Built to be forked
highlights.description: The project intentionally favors a small, readable structure over configurability, making it a fast base to copy and restyle for new personal or template sites.
